title: add-async-kernel-latency-sampler-and-batching-simulator-microbench
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: We need lower-overhead, continuous visibility into per-kernel submission and queueing latency across the runtime's async execution path to diagnose intermittent tail latency regressions observed in Dedicated. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) an async kernel latency sampler that attaches lightweight samples to the kernel submission path and aggregates histograms for export; and 2) a microbenchmarking binary (batching-simulator) that models continuous batching + KV-cache warmup behavior to validate scheduler heuristics.

What changed (high level): added a low-cost sampling ring buffer and histogram aggregation in runtime/metrics, instrumented major async submission points with conditional NVTX ranges (behind a runtime flag to avoid production overhead), and added a standalone microbench under tools/batch-sim to simulate mixed-size requests, KV-cache hits, and different batching window sizes. Also added Grafana dashboard json and Prometheus scrape hooks to visualize the new histograms.

Why this approach: previous profiling artifacts were either too heavy (full-trace CUPTI capture) or too coarse (per-request counters). The sampler uses stochastic sampling at a tunable rate, a compact per-GPU ring buffer, and periodic aggregation to HDR histograms to keep cost <0.5% CPU for typical loads. The batching-simulator lets us stress scheduler heuristics offline to validate improvements before rolling to prod.

Key implementation notes: - sampling ring buffer: runtime/metrics/sampler_ring.{h,cpp} - aggregation worker runs in the stats thread and emits HDR histograms via prometheus/client (runtime/observability/hdr_exporter.cpp) - NVTX ranges introduced via a thin macro NVTX_SCOPE_SAFE that compiles to no-op unless ENABLE_RUNTIME_NVTX is set; this keeps binary overhead minimal - batching-simulator: tools/batch-sim/* (config-driven scenarios, manifests included) - added end-to-end unit+integration tests: tests/metrics_sampler_test.cpp and tools/batch-sim/integration_test.py - new dashboards: observability/dashboards/grafana/gpu_kernel_latency_sampler.json

Microbench results (selected): Using a 16-GPU staging cluster and a mixed prompt workload: - baseline (no sampler, old scheduler): p50=28ms, p90=92ms, p99=210ms - with sampler enabled (sampling rate=0.02) and scheduler unchanged: p50=28ms, p90=91ms, p99=208ms (overhead within noise) - with scheduler heuristics tuned (compact window + kv-warmup enabled) validated via batch-sim: p50=26ms, p90=85ms, p99=178ms (approx 2.9% p50 and 15% p99 improvement in this workload) Detailed raw outputs are under tools/batch-sim/benchmarks/2025-11-17-*/

Backward-compat & rollout: features are guarded behind runtime flags (enable_kernel_sampler, enable_nvtx_scopes, batching_sim_mode). Default flags are off. We will stage in canary with sampling rate 0.01, verify metrics and dashboards, then enable sampling on Dedicated clusters if stable.

Checklist: - [x] core sampler implementation - [x] NVTX macros and conditional scopes - [x] prometheus export and Grafana dashboard - [x] batching-simulator and scenario manifests - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs: observability/README.md updated

Files changed (high level): runtime/metrics/sampler_ring.h, runtime/metrics/sampler_ring.cpp, runtime/metrics/hdr_exporter.cpp, runtime/metrics/hdr_exporter.h, runtime/observability/nvtx_wrapper.h, runtime/observability/nvtx_wrapper.cpp, runtime/execution/async_submit.cpp (instrumented), runtime/scheduler/heuristics.cpp (compact window heuristic), tools/batch-sim/main.cpp, tools/batch-sim/configs/mixed_prompt.yaml, tools/batch-sim/README.md, tools/batch-sim/benchmarks/collector.py, tests/metrics_sampler_test.cpp, tests/batch_sim_integration.py, observability/dashboards/grafana/gpu_kernel_latency_sampler.json, docs/observability/README.md

Commits (summary): - add sampler ring buffer and HDR aggregation - wire sampler into submission path with safe NVTX scopes - add prometheus exporter and dashboard - batching-simulator initial implementation + scenarios - tests and docs - fix: reduce memory churn in ring buffer allocation

Review notes and decisions: - NVTX scopes: reviewers asked for a low-overhead guard; implemented NVTX_SCOPE_SAFE with compile and runtime guards. - Aggregation cadence: tuned to 5s by default after perf review to balance freshness and CPU usage. - Histogram resolution: HDR with configurable sigfigs; default 3 significant digits chosen as tradeoff.

Release notes: "Added an optional async kernel latency sampler and batching-simulator microbench. New Grafana dashboard for per-kernel latency. Feature gated; no default runtime change."

Risk/rollout plan: low risk (flag-gated). Canary rollout plan included in docs/observability/README.md.

References: ENG-3412, ENG-3459, earlier CUpti/ebpf PRs for heavy traces (for context).
